Title: Zetrix AI sinks to five sen as RM2bil sukuk covenant breach looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd shares hit a fresh low of five sen on Friday as the embattled technology company faces a potential breach of its RM2 billion sukuk covenant, adding to a string of setbacks in recent months.
At market close, the stock had pared some losses to settle at 5.5 sen, still down 15.38 per cent from Thursday's close of 6.5 sen.
It was Bursa Malaysia's most actively traded counter, with nearly 255 million shares changing hands.
At 5.5 sen, Zetrix AI had a market capitalisation of about RM444.33 million.
The latest sell-off came after Zetrix AI disclosed that its managing director, Wong Thean Soon, was no longer the company's single largest shareholder following forced share sales by banks.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said Wong's combined direct and indirect shareholding had fallen to 1.895 per cent as at Oct 15.
Under the terms of its RM2 billion Sukuk Wakalah programme, Wong is required to remain the company's single largest shareholder, directly or indirectly.
Zetrix AI has until Oct 22 to remedy the potential breach, failing which it will seek consent or directions from sukukholders through an extraordinary resolution.
The company said it was in discussions with the sukuk trustee and would announce any material developments.
Bursa Malaysia temporarily suspended trading in Zetrix AI's securities at 9.19am on Friday following the announcement.
The latest development adds to mounting pressure on Zetrix AI, whose shares have plunged 93.3 per cent from their April high of 89.5 sen.
On Aug 28, the stock plunged about 50 per cent amid forced sales of shares pledged by Wong.
Concerns over Wong's shrinking shareholding and the company's rising borrowings subsequently prompted MARC Ratings to place its RM2 billion Islamic medium-term notes programme on MARCWatch Developing in September.
The rating agency highlighted the sharp increase in Zetrix AI's borrowings, which rose to RM2.2 billion as at June 2026 from RM160.5 million in 2021.
Its cumulative development expenditure also climbed to RM3.7 billion from RM322.5 million over the same period, accounting for about 56 per cent of total assets.
MARC Ratings subsequently revised the company's MARCWatch status to "Negative" in early October, citing concerns over transparency, governance and insufficient information on its borrowings and development expenditure.
The revision followed the resignation of Zetrix AI's external auditor, TGS TW, in late September.
The company also faced another setback this month when the Road Transport Department suspended its services from Oct 5 over outstanding remittances.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the outstanding collections amounted to RM314 million, while Zetrix AI submitted a proposal to resolve the matter.
The succession of setbacks has overshadowed the company's expansion into artificial intelligence and blockchain technology, despite its reported net profit of about RM540 million in the first half of 2026.

Title: Tuanku Muhriz has stern words with Negri MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir having a stern word with Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim amid the state's constitutional crisis has gone viral.
In the clip, taken after Friday prayers at a mosque in Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz is heard telling Ismail that he does not want to see him.
The ruler is also heard expressing his dissatisfaction with Ismail and former state executive council members over a letter to the Keeper of the Rulers' Seal stating that he was no longer the state ruler.
Ismail is seen acknowledging Tuanku Muhriz and paying homage to the ruler.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Ismail for comment.
In a separate video, Tuanku Muhriz is seen refusing to shake Ismail's hand upon arriving at a mosque.
On Sept 13, Ismail said that an April 19 proclamation by the former Undangs removing Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan had been approved by the state administration.
He said the decision was unanimously endorsed by all members of the state executive council at its meeting.
The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) later said the menteri besar and state executive council did not have the unilateral power to remove the ruler or declare the position vacant.
It said the validity and legal effect of the April 19 proclamation must be determined through the constitutional and legal process under the Negri Sembilan Constitution.
A week later, Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors.
Earlier today, Tuanku Muhriz conferred the state's
prestigious honours
on three Undangs and their consorts at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here yesterday.
The three Undangs, Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari of Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi of Luak Jelebu and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid of Luak Rembau, were conferred the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS).

Title: PeKa B40 to be rebranded as PeKa Sihat
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has agreed to rebrand the PeKa B40 programme as PeKa Sihat, with measures being drawn up to improve its effectiveness and ease congestion at public health clinics.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Health Ministry was coordinating several proposed changes, including the use of premises and clinics participating in the programme.
"The cabinet agreed to amend the Health Ministry's PeKa B40 programme, taking into account its effectiveness in addressing non-communicable diseases.
"The programme will be rebranded as PeKa Sihat, and the Health Ministry will announce the details in due course," he said at his weekly post-cabinet press conference here today.
PeKa B40, established under the Health Ministry and administered by ProtectHealth Corporation, offers several benefits, including health screenings, medical equipment assistance worth up to RM20,000, cancer treatment incentives and transport allowances.
The programme is automatically available to eligible Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah recipients aged 40 and above.

Title: Azalina to hold more talks with parliamentary committee on AG-Public Prosecutor Separation Bill
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has been directed to hold further discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee on the proposed constitutional amendments to separate the roles of the Attorney-General (A-G) and Public Prosecutor (PP).
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim issued the directive following several matters raised by the Malay Rulers during the Conference of Rulers on the proposed amendments.
"The prime minister has directed Azalina to hold engagement sessions and discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee, which prepared the draft constitutional amendments.
"Any further amendments or improvements must then be communicated to the Conference of Rulers," he said at a post-cabinet press conference here today.
Fahmi said the cabinet was also briefed on the Parliamentary Service Council, which has assumed full responsibility for Parliament, with the executive no longer having jurisdiction over the institution.
He said the move fulfilled a reform pledge and marked a significant step towards strengthening democracy in the country.
"During this transition period, several matters need to be examined, and the cabinet will continue to provide assistance if any issues need to be addressed.
"However, jurisdiction over Parliament, the Dewan Rakyat and the Dewan Negara now rests entirely with the Parliamentary Service Council," he said.
Fahmi said Anwar had also briefed the cabinet on his audience with the Malay Rulers during the Conference of Rulers on the proposed constitutional amendment to limit the Prime Minister's term of office.
He said the proposed term limit and the separation of the Attorney-General's and Public Prosecutor's roles were two major institutional reform initiatives, although some details still needed to be refined.
The
Parliamentary Service Act 2025
and related amendments to the Federal Constitution took effect on Oct 1.
Azalina was previously reported as saying that the
Bills to limit a prime minister's tenure
to 10 years and separate the powers of the AG and PP had been completed.
She said the Bills could be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat at any time.
The
Bill to limit the prime minister's tenure
to 10 years had previously failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Dewan Rakyat.
It received 146 votes in favour, while 44 MPs abstained and 32 were absent.
Meanwhile, the Bill to separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor was referred to a Parliamentary Special Select Committee for further scrutiny.

Title: Miti to expand markets, strengthen Malaysia's export performance under 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) will continue to expand and strengthen Malaysia's export markets through initiatives under the 2027 Budget.
Deputy Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Miti, through the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, would lead export-strengthening initiatives through the RM60 million Export Capacity Building Programme and the RM50 million Export Strengthening and Market Diversification Fund.
The initiatives would also be supported by RM1 billion in financing facilities from Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd and RM10 million through EXIM Bank.
"Through 200 export promotion activities, the programme is expected to directly benefit more than 3,500 local companies, with export sales targeted to reach RM12 billion by the end of 2027," he said in a statement.
The deputy minister said efforts to facilitate business would also be intensified through collaboration between the Malaysia Productivity Corporation and the Special Task Force on Agency Reform to reduce bureaucratic red tape.
He revealed that the regulatory reform initiative had so far helped save industries RM3.71 billion in compliance costs and expedite business licence approvals.
Sim said Miti is also focusing on developing viable regional industrial clusters to promote balanced economic growth nationwide. The comprehensive and integrated implementation of these initiatives was expected to enhance Malaysia's standing as a leading regional investment destination and a sustainable global trade hub.
"These efforts include the ministry's strategic initiatives to drive the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, develop automotive and maritime hubs in Perak, and strengthen the semiconductor chip technology ecosystem in Penang and Kedah," he added.
"They also involve expanding trade corridor infrastructure in Perlis and developing a planning framework for a Special Economic Zone in Sibu, Sarawak."

Title: Duta Enclave: Govt overpaid up to RM500,000 in land compensation, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government may have overpaid by up to RM500,000 in compensation for the disputed Duta Enclave land and may not need to pay anything more, the High Court heard today.
Government-appointed valuer Tan Tat Khuan said his assessment showed that the government had overpaid by between RM400,000 and RM500,000 when it compensated the company for the land acquired in 1956.
He said his valuation placed the compensation at between RM875,000 and RM985,000, compared with the approximately RM1.39 million previously paid by the government.
"If the court agrees with my calculation of RM875,000, no additional compensation needs to be paid," he said.
Tan, 40, an assistant director at the Valuation and Property Services Department under the Finance Ministry, said this when questioned by senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan before High Court judge Roslan Mat Nor.
He said the two valuations were based on different land areas used in the assessment, resulting in different rates per hectare.
Tan said his first valuation placed the land's value at RM875,000, while the second put it at RM985,000.
He maintained that both figures were lower than the compensation already paid by the government.
However, Tan acknowledged that the government could be required to pay an additional RM1.2 million if the court accepted the valuation submitted by Semantan Estate's private valuer.
He said the private valuation amounted to approximately RM2.62 million, compared with the RM1.39 million previously paid by the government.
The Court of Appeal had previously directed that any additional compensation should take into account interest.
During cross-examination by the company's lawyer Janet Chai, Tan also acknowledged that he could not independently verify the development restrictions applicable to the land in 1956 as the original planning records could not be located.
Chai questioned Tan over his reliance on historical valuation reports prepared by two other valuers, Wragg and Harding, which indicated that development on the land was restricted to residential houses at a density of one house per acre.
Tan agreed that he had not produced any original planning documents to independently verify the restriction.
He said checks with PlanMalaysia had failed to locate the planning records from 1956.
However, Tan maintained that the historical reports were reliable as both valuers had conducted checks at the time and reached consistent findings.
Roslan then asked whether there was a possibility that the reports contained errors.
Tan replied that he was not saying the reports were 100 per cent accurate, but maintained that they could be relied upon.
He also disagreed with Chai's suggestion that the reports amounted to hearsay.
He explained that although he could not verify the planning information against original records, he had relied on the historical reports as references in preparing his own valuation.
The proceedings concern the assessment of compensation payable to Semantan Estate following the Court of Appeal's decision on the disputed Duta Enclave land.
The dispute dates back to 1956, when the government took possession of the 263.272-acre land, which now houses several government buildings and public facilities.
The Court of Appeal had ruled that the land should remain with the government, with Semantan Estate entitled to compensation to be assessed based on its value at the time of acquisition.

Title: Malaysia needs to upskill, digitalise MSMEs to boost growth, wages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to accelerate the upskilling and digitalisation of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to strengthen their contribution to economic growth and ensure workers benefit more from rising productivity, said Nottingham University Malaysia economist Dr Tan Shih-Ming.
He said MSMEs account for about 91 per cent of businesses in Malaysia, employ about 50 per cent of the workforce, and contribute around 40 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), making them a significant part of the economy.
"So Malaysia has to find ways of upskilling and digitalising MSMEs moving forward so that they could actually contribute to larger economic growth for the country as a result," he said in an interview on Bernama World's programme, "Budget 2027: Malaysia's Growth and Global Competitiveness".
Tan said Malaysia's economic growth was expected to moderate after this year's strong export performance, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and electrical and electronics (E&E), which contributed to a 30 per cent increase in exports.
He said geopolitical uncertainties, shipping and insurance costs, and potential changes to United States tariffs could affect Malaysia's exports and growth prospects, while a slowdown in the AI sector could also weigh on the country's semiconductor and E&E industries.
He added that Malaysia needed to strengthen its capabilities in semiconductor testing, assembly, design and innovation, as its reliance on external technology could leave the economy vulnerable to international developments.
On wages, Tan said productivity among firms had increased substantially, but workers were not necessarily paid commensurately, with some holding qualifications higher than those required for their jobs.
"The government's minimum wage policy and efforts to raise wages for semi-skilled workers are positive steps, saying workers should receive better pay as their productivity improves," he said.
However, Tan cautioned that wage increases needed to be balanced against the risk of higher prices and inflation, requiring careful implementation of minimum wage policies.
"Economic growth was also uneven across sectors, with AI and semiconductors driving expansion while other industries grew more slowly, meaning workers did not benefit equally from rising economic activity.
"As a result, workers outside high-productivity sectors might not experience comparable wage increases, underscoring the importance of upskilling and aligning the education system with changing industry requirements," he added.
Tan said improving job opportunities and wages would take time and require sufficient investment as Malaysia continued to develop its capabilities in emerging technology sectors.
He added that lower inflation did not mean prices were falling but rather they were rising at a slower pace, while wage growth might still lag behind the rising cost of living.
On cash assistance, Tan said cash assistance under the 2027 Budget could provide short-term relief to households but sustained improvements in living standards would depend on higher wages and stronger productivity among businesses.
"Malaysia needed to build long-term economic resilience against external shocks, adding that upskilling workers and digitalising MSMEs would be important to strengthening productivity and ensuring more sustainable economic growth," he said.

Title: Singapore and China can drive regional growth in digital, green sectors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Singapore and China can work together to strengthen development across Southeast Asia, with digitalisation and the green economy identified as key areas for bilateral and regional cooperation.
Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong, who is also Trade and Industry Minister, said both countries could build on decades of cooperation to strengthen capabilities in Singapore and across Asean.
"Singapore and China have spent decades building trust through mutually beneficial cooperation. We should now draw on that trust to build capabilities in Singapore and across Asean," he said.
Speaking at the annual FutureChina Global Forum on Sept 25, Gan said connectivity and openness had been important drivers of Asia's growth, but geopolitical rivalries were putting pressure on them.
With businesses and workers concerned about being left behind, economies risked turning inward and adopting protectionist measures, he said.
"We have to make openness work better for businesses and for people… Resilience requires us to build stronger capabilities at home, while expanding our connections abroad."
BILATERAL PARTNERSHIP
Gan said bilateral agreements between Singapore and China provided businesses with greater certainty, while both countries had a track record of industrial and connectivity projects.
"China is pursuing innovation and industrial upgrading, while Singapore is sharpening our own economic strategy and developing new sources of growth," he said at the forum, organised by government-linked non-profit Business China.
"We can combine our complementary strengths and seize emerging opportunities together."
He identified artificial intelligence (AI) as an area for closer collaboration, citing the Singapore-China Digital Policy Dialogue as a platform for exchanging views on AI governance.
Companies and research institutions could also work together to develop business applications for AI, he said.
Singapore had also signed agreements with China to establish green and digital shipping corridors at municipal, provincial and national levels.
"China has deep technological and manufacturing capabilities, while Singapore brings strengths in areas such as finance, connectivity and project implementation," Gan said.
REGIONAL GROWTH
Gan said the benefits of Singapore-China cooperation should extend across Southeast Asia, adding that greater regional prosperity would also benefit businesses.
"A stronger and more resilient Asean should be a shared priority for Singapore and China," he said.
He stressed that industrial upgrading should go beyond trade and investment to include local enterprises and workers in capability-building efforts.
Referring to commitments on the digital and green economies, as well as supply-chain connectivity under upgrades to the Asean-China Free Trade Area, Gan said these pledges should translate into practical opportunities for businesses and workers.
"The aim is not for every economy to do exactly the same thing. It is for businesses across the region to build a competitive niche in value chains, and for workers to see pathways to progress," he said.
"That is how regional integration becomes more relevant and resilient."
Gan added that Singapore would work to deepen integration within Asean when it assumes the bloc's chairmanship in 2027.
"We want an Asean that remains open to the world, with the capabilities, connections and agency to be able to shape our own future," he said.

Title: Seven foreigners claim trial over Forest City crypto scam
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Seven Chinese men, including three students, claimed trial at the magistrates' court here today to conspiring to cheat through a fictitious cryptocurrency investment scheme at Forest City earlier this month.
The accused — Hong Wei Xian, 25; Zhou Fu, 22; Chen Lu, 23; Yuan Shuping, 29; Li Yi, 30; Wang Tengfei, 30; and Chen Xiaojia, 33 — pleaded not guilty after the charges were read to them in Mandarin before magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab.
They were jointly charged with conspiring to carry out a fraudulent investment scheme involving non-existent cryptocurrency at two residential units in Forest City at noon on Oct 1.
The charge was framed under Section 120B(2) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 417 of the same code, which deals with cheating and carries a maximum six-month jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Sarah Siti Aisyah Mustapha Kamal proposed bail of RM15,000 for each accused, with two local sureties.
Lawyer Lim Tyng Chieh, representing Yuan, Li, Wang and Chen Xiaojia, sought lower bail, saying his clients were independent contractors with permanent addresses at Forest City.
Lawyer Pang Yong Tong, representing Hong, Zhou and Chen Lu, also sought lower bail, citing the student status of three of the accused and their residence at Forest City.
The court allowed each accused bail of RM7,000 with two local sureties and fixed Nov 11 for mention for the submission of documents.
In a separate charge before the same court, Hong also pleaded not guilty to entering Malaysia without a valid pass.
He was charged under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, punishable under Section 6(3) of the same Act, which provides for a fine of up to RM10,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both, and up to six strokes of the cane upon conviction.
The court granted him bail of RM9,000 with two sureties.
Meanwhile, Zhou and Chen Lu faced similar immigration charges before a separate magistrate's court.
Magistrate A Shaarmini fixed Nov 2 for a further bail application, pending verification of the two accused's travel documents by the prosecution.

Title: Malaysian businesses, umrah agencies cautious after Riyadh airport attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian businesses and umrah agencies have adopted a cautious approach to their operations in the Middle East amid security concerns following a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh last week.
The Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) said Malaysian companies in the retail and consumer sectors in the region had adopted measures to adapt to the current situation.
"Based on the latest updates from our Trade Office in Jeddah, Malaysian businesses in the retail and consumer sectors remain cautious and have adopted measures to adapt to the current situation.
"Increased logistics insurance premiums, fewer tourists and pilgrims, volatile flight schedules and shifts in consumer spending could affect their businesses," it said in a reply to Business Times.
Citing the latest statistics from Saudi Arabia's General Authority for Statistics as at Dec 31, 2024, Matrade said Malaysia's foreign direct investment in the kingdom stood at SAR2.86 billion (US$760 million).
By value, most Malaysian businesses in Saudi Arabia operate in industrial products and services, including precast and building materials, construction services, facilities management and utilities.
"Nevertheless, it would be premature to draw conclusions at this stage. However, a prolonged escalation could pose challenges to trade, particularly in logistics, shipping routes, delivery timelines and associated costs.
"We will continue to monitor the situation and gather feedback from the business community. Recovery in these sectors will depend on the swift mitigation and resolution of regional geopolitical tensions," Matrade said.
A Houthi strike hit Riyadh's international airport on Oct 12, a day after an attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations there.
The previous day's attack was reported to be the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade and marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war.
Following the attacks, the Malaysian government advised a temporary halt to travel to Saudi Arabia for umrah due to security concerns.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was previously quoted as saying that the missile attack in Riyadh had prompted the government to advise Malaysians to defer non-essential travel to Makkah and Madinah for the time being.
Meanwhile, Pertubuhan Agensi Umrah dan Haji Sarawak (Suha) chairman Ruzaiman Ghazalee said some airlines had cancelled umrah flights before the Riyadh airport attack, prompting several umrah agencies in Sarawak to switch to other airlines.
"However, so far, Malaysia Airlines, Saudia, AirAsia and other airlines have continued operating their flights. In general, most umrah packages are still proceeding as planned, although a few agencies have postponed their trips," he said.
Following the attack, some Suha member agencies received requests to postpone umrah trips, including departures scheduled for December, mainly due to safety concerns, he added.
He said the situation had heightened customers' concerns and made travel planning more challenging.
"For umrah trips, last-minute changes are not easy, as flights, hotels and other arrangements are usually booked in advance.
"Agencies also have to consider additional costs and other practical issues.
"Overall, the Middle East conflict has had some impact on the umrah industry in Sarawak and Malaysia. For now, our main priority remains the safety and welfare of pilgrims," Ruzaiman added.

Title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Review needed for rescue, firefighting operations at Long Lellang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department (Rela) personnel based at the Long Lellang STOLport rushed into action to battle the flames when the Bo-105 helicopter crashed there on Sept 8.
They were joined by people from nearby villages, but despite their best efforts, the fire continued to blaze for several hours, even after completely using up all their fire extinguishers.
The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB), however, noted that the Rela personnel were not wearing firefighting personal protective equipment (PPEs).
In its preliminary report, the bureau said Rela personnel who were on duty at the STOLport, approached the crash site carrying portable fire extinguishers.
"Several villagers subsequently joined the effort to put out the fire and assist the occupants, with additional personnel arriving minutes later to support the emergency response and rescue operation.
"However, the fire continued to burn for several hours despite efforts to extinguish it using all 12 dry powder fire extinguishers available at the airstrip's terminal," it said.
It added that the equipment comprised five 50kg extinguishers and seven 9kg units.
"Although firefighting PPE was available at the STOLport, an examination after the crash found visible deterioration and damage to some equipment, particularly the protective clothing.
"Rescue and firefighting duties at the airstrip had been assigned to Aviation Security (Avsec) Rela personnel acting as auxiliary rescue and firefighting personnel. However, no dedicated rescue and firefighting personnel were stationed at the STOLport," it said.
As part of its immediate safety action recommendations, the AAIB called on the aerodrome operator to review rescue and firefighting arrangements at its STOLports.
The review should ensure auxiliary personnel were appropriately trained and equipped, and that firefighting equipment and PPE were properly maintained and serviceable.
The helicopter, which was conducting a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight, just short of the runway at Long Lellang STOLport, killing the pilot and four medical personnel on board.

Title: Cable thief caught red-handed along NKVE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A cable thief has been arrested following a joint operation by Plus Malaysia Bhd (Plus) personnel and police along the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE).
Plus said the arrest was made during a recent operation to curb the theft and destruction of critical highway infrastructure.
In a Facebook post, the highway concessionaire said the suspect was handed over to the Sentul police headquarters for further investigation.
"Through our continued commitment, the Plus team, in cooperation with police, successfully arrested a suspect involved in cable theft activities along the NKVE during a recent operation," it said.
Photographs shared by Plus showed two uniformed policemen beside a patrol car parked on the highway shoulder at night.
A man was seen sitting on the ground near a guardrail with his hands held behind his back as the policemen attended to the situation.
Other photographs showed cutting tools, including a cordless power tool, a hacksaw, a hand saw and a toolbox, alongside a severed cable on a concrete roadside barrier.
Plus did not disclose the date of the operation, the suspect's identity or the quantity and value of the cables involved.
The concessionaire said the theft or destruction of highway facilities was a serious offence that could endanger motorists.
It said damage to cables, safety barriers and road signs could compromise highway safety systems and disrupt their operations.
Plus also thanked the personnel involved in the operation for helping safeguard highway infrastructure.
It urged motorists to report suspicious activities along expressways to help prevent such crimes.
Members of the public with information can contact PLUSLine at 1-800-88-0000 or alert the authorities.

Title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Pilot medically fit, aircraft was airworthy, weather conditions good
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The pilot of the Bo-105 helicopter which crashed and killed five people in Long Lellang on Sept 8, was medically fit and properly licensed, while the aircraft was deemed airworthy.
The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) in its preliminary report found that 30-year-old Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, from Seremban, had 1,825.5 flight hours under his belt, including 915 hours and 50 minutes on the Bo-105 helicopter type.
The AAIB report said the Zainol had logged 81 hours and 48 minutes of flying time in the 90 days before the Sept 8 crash, while his rest period before the final flight was 22 hours.
"He held a valid Commercial Pilot Licence (Helicopter), with an aircraft rating for the Bo-105, and his licence was valid until Jan 31, 2027.
"He had also undergone a medical examination on Jan 26 this year, with his medical certificate valid until Jan 31, 2027.
"The pilot held the appropriate licence, qualifications, and approvals required to conduct the flight in accordance with the applicable regulations, held a valid medical certificate, and was medically fit to conduct the flight," the report read.
It also confirmed that the helicopter held valid Certificates of Registration and Airworthiness and was determined to be airworthy at the time.
"The aircraft, an MBB-Bo105 S manufactured by Eurocopter Deutschland GmbH in 1991, bore registration number 9M-LLF and serial number S-867. It was owned by Rotorwing (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd.
"Its Certificate of Registration was valid until July 28, 2029, while its Certificate of Airworthiness was valid until Aug 4, 2027," it said.
The report also stated that good weather conditions were reported and no distress call recorded before the accident.
It said all communication frequencies were operating normally throughout the flight.
Citing a weather assessment by the Malaysian Meteorological Department, the AAIB report said conditions around the airstrip were generally good, with visibility exceeding 10km at the time.
"Radar and satellite imagery showed no significant thunderstorm or rainfall activity within 20 nautical miles of the airstrip between 8am and 3pm.
"However, moderate convective cloud activity was observed in the area from about 4pm onwards," read the report.
It added that surface wind observations were available for Long Lellang STOLport, but no aerodrome or wind shear warnings were issued.
The report also said no significant meteorological information (SIGMET) or airmen's meteorological information (AIRMET) was active within 20 nautical miles of the airstrip.
AAIB said the helicopter had made several stops along the way from Miri to Long Lellang.
"According to operational information and Spider Track flight-tracking records, the helicopter started up at 10.15am before departing Miri at 10.24am for Ba'Lai.
"It landed at Ba'Lai at 11.39am, where the helicopter was shut down. It later resumed operations at 1.36pm, departing for Selungo," read the report.
It said the helicopter landed in Selungo at 2.02pm and was shut down before being refuelled in preparation for the next flight.
"It started up again at 3.17pm and departed for Long Lellang STOLport.
"The last recorded position in the Spider Track data was at 3.27pm, when the helicopter was approximately three nautical miles from Long Lellang STOLport," it said.
Spider Track is a satellite-based flight tracking and safety system for aircraft. It uses a small cockpit hardware device connected to the satellite network to transmit real-time data like an aircraft's GPS location, speed, and altitude back to a live digital map on the ground.
The report said no "abnormal event" had been identified throughout the flight, though the the helicopter's operational and technical status during the first sector (Miri to Ba'Lai) remained subject to further verification.
A 37-second video recording taken by a person on the ground captured the final portion of the flight, showing the helicopter with a visible trail of smoke and apparent flames near the area aft of the main gearbox, though it did not capture the point of impact.
"When the first responders approached the accident site, the helicopter was engulfed in fire approximately 25 metres of the Runway 04 threshold," the report said.
It added that the helicopter was substantially destroyed by the fire with the AAIB saying the origin, development and sequence of the fire remained under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Preliminary report released, no cause found yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than a month after a Bo-105 helicopter went down in Long Lellang on Sept 8, claiming five lives, investigators have yet to reach a conclusion on what caused the crash.
The preliminary report released by the Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) states the safety investigation remained ongoing, with the available factual data still only at a preliminary stage.
"Continuous fact-finding regarding flight operations, standard operating practices, and helicopter maintenance history will provide the necessary evidence to validate system defences and evaluate any latent conditions," the report read.
It found, at this preliminary stage, no fault with the helicopter's airframe, its maintenance nor the pilot.
However, it pointed out that the helicopter's engines were sent to the manufacturer's facility for further examination, with the powerplant investigation ongoing and any airworthiness implications for other engines of the same type yet to be established.
The report said an engineer from the engine manufacturer had participated in the on-site investigation as a technical expert representing the engine's state of design and state of manufacture.
"A detailed examination of the remaining wreckage was conducted, with particular attention given to the powerplant and its associated components.
"The recovered powerplant components were subsequently transported to the engine manufacturer's facility for further examination and analysis," it said.
The helicopter was fitted with two Rolls-Royce 250-C20B engines, with the No. 1 engine manufactured in 1989 and the No. 2 engine in 1976.
The AAIB said a 37-second ground-based video recording of the final portion of the flight showed a visible smoke trail and apparent flames in the vicinity of the area aft of the main gearbox with the origin, development and sequence of the fire remaining under investigation.
The report also said an initial examination of the accident site indicated that the helicopter sustained substantial damage from fire and ground contact.
The main wreckage and associated debris were found in the immediate vicinity of the crash site, while smaller items and components detached from the helicopter were recovered for further examination and analysis.
The report said the extent of damage to the airframe, engines, transmission system, flight controls and other helicopter components remained subject to further detailed examination with all recovered components and debris were transported to Miri for further analysis.
"A detailed wreckage examination will be conducted to establish the nature and extent of the damage and, where possible, the sequence and development of the fire and ground-contact damage," the report said.
The AAIB also said the helicopter was deemed airworthy at the time and held valid Certificates of Registration and Airworthiness.
It added that findings of the detailed wreckage examination and engine analysis will be included in the final report.
On Sept 8, a Flying Doctor Service Bo-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near Long Lellang STOLport in Sarawak, killing all on board.

Title: Protecting young lungs: Why proper masks matter during haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parents should not underestimate the health risks posed by prolonged exposure to haze, particularly its potential impact on children's lung development.
Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Faculty of Health Sciences senior lecturer Dr Noor Haziqah Kamaludin said children's respiratory systems continued to develop into their early 20s, making them more vulnerable to air pollution.
She said children breathed faster to meet their bodies' higher oxygen demands.
"Outdoor activities without proper face masks during haze expose children to harmful particles that could disrupt the development of new alveoli in the lungs.
"Prolonged exposure could impair lung development and increase the risk of chronic asthma, recurrent bronchitis and persistent respiratory allergies," she said when contacted today.
Haziqah urged parents to watch for early signs of respiratory problems, including persistent dry coughs, particularly at night or after physical activity, rapid breathing, wheezing, fatigue, loss of appetite, headaches and eye irritation.
She said parents should seek immediate medical attention if their children experienced severe breathing difficulties, including chest retractions, gasping for air, or pale lips and fingernails.
She advised vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and those with existing respiratory conditions, to limit outdoor activities and remain indoors with adequate ventilation and air filtration.
"Those with respiratory conditions should carry their prescribed inhalers when going outdoors and continue taking their medication as directed by their doctors.
"People should avoid strenuous outdoor activities, as these increase the amount of polluted air inhaled. Staying adequately hydrated is also important," she said.
Haziqah said ordinary surgical masks offered limited protection against fine haze particles because they did not provide an airtight seal.
She recommended properly fitted N95, KN95 or KF94 respirators, which are designed to filter at least 94 to 95 per cent of particles.
"For children, parents should ensure the mask fits their faces properly to prevent air leakage around the edges, while the nose clip should be secured firmly.
"A properly fitted mask should move slightly inwards when inhaling and outwards when exhaling," she said.
Haziqah advised against wearing tight-fitting masks continuously for more than two hours, citing concerns about breathing resistance and fatigue, particularly among vulnerable individuals.
She said masks should be replaced when they became damp, dirty or difficult to breathe through.

Title: Fashion Valet received nearly RM40mil from Khazanah, PNB in 2018, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court was told today that Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd received nearly RM40 million in investment funds from Khazanah Nasional Bhd (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) in 2018.
Bukit Damansara Public Bank Bhd banking services manager Tay Lay Hong, 54, said the amount involved four transactions recorded between March and December that year.
"An examination of the company's bank statements showed that Khazanah transferred RM7.84 million on March 23, 2018, and RM11.74 million on March 26, 2018.
"PNB recorded transfers of RM11.95 million on June 4, 2018, and RM8.36 million on Dec 20, 2018," he said.
The fifth prosecution witness was testifying in the trial of Fashion Valet founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, who were charged with criminal breach of trust involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB.
During today's proceedings, Tay also confirmed an RM11 million withdrawal from Fashion Valet's account on Aug 21, 2018, recorded as "PAYNET DIRECT DEBIT".
"I confirm that this was a fund disbursement transaction carried out through bulk payments online.
"The RM11 million transfer fell under a category of payments requiring verification and approval by an authorised person for the Public Bank account held under Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd.
"However, I am unsure who the authorised person for online banking was. To my knowledge, the appointment of an authorised person is based on a directors' resolution, and the authorised signatory is usually the same person authorised to conduct online banking transactions," he said.
Tay, who joined Public Bank in 1993, said a RM5 million transaction from 30 Maple Sdn Bhd was credited to Fadzarudin's personal account on Sept 4, 2018.
"The transaction was recorded with the reference 'Interim Dividend'," he said.
He also confirmed that RM5 million was transferred from 30 Maple to Vivy Sofinas' personal account on Sept 3, 2018, with the reference "CIMB Rentas".
The two transactions brought the total amount credited to their personal accounts to RM10 million.
The bank statements referred to by Tay also recorded RM5.5 million in cash withdrawals over the counter from the personal accounts of Vivy Sofinas and Fadzarudin on Sept 5, 2018.
However, Tay clarified that the withdrawals were made at Public Bank branch 269, not the Bukit Damansara branch, which has the branch code 066.
During cross-examination by lawyer Datuk M. Athimulan, Tay agreed that all the information in his witness statement was based on bank statements.
He also agreed that the RM11 million withdrawn from Fashion Valet's bank account did not necessarily mean the money was transferred to a single personal account, adding that bulk payments could cover salaries, shop rentals and other expenses.
Vivy Sofinas, 38, and Fadzarudin, 37, were jointly charged, in their capacity as Fashion Valet directors, with criminal breach of trust for making an RM8 million payment from the company's bank account to 30 Maple without the approval of Fashion Valet's board of directors.
The offence was allegedly committed at Public Bank's Bukit Damansara branch at 36-40 Medan Setia 2, Plaza Damansara, on Aug 21, 2018.
They were charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code. If convicted, they face imprisonment of between two and 20 years, whipping and a possible fine.

Title: [UPDATED]: Anwar to discuss haze at special meeting on Monday
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will chair a special meeting on Monday to discuss several issues, including the haze currently affecting the country.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the High-Level Committee (HLC) meeting on National Disaster Management would, among others, focus on the need for better coordination among ministries to address the haze impact.
He said this included outdoor sporting activities and school operations and other educational institutions.
"The Education Ministry and Health Ministry had informed the cabinet that existing guidelines to address the haze were based on the National Haze Action Plan, which was currently in force.
"The prime minister will chair a meeting on Monday, and the haze issue will be among the matters discussed.
"Further information will be provided after Monday's meeting, including by the Health Ministry, Education Ministry and Youth and Sports Ministry," he said at his weekly post-cabinet press conference here today.

Title: [UPDATED] No Malaysian plantation firms linked to Indonesia forest fires, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: No Malaysian plantation companies with oil palm concessions in Indonesia have been found to be involved in forest fires linked to the haze.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said cross-checks with Malaysian companies showed that most of the fires observed had occurred outside concessions owned by Malaysian firms.
"There was one plantation owned by a Malaysian company, Genting Plantations, where a fire had spread from outside the plantation rather than originating within it.
"The fire has since been put out," he said at his weekly post-cabinet press conference here today.
Fahmi said the Malaysian Palm Oil Board would continue to engage with Malaysian plantation companies operating in Indonesia.
[[nid:1556835]]
He said parts of Kalimantan had gone more than 101 days without rain, with little rainfall recorded during that period.
Asked about Indonesia's response to offers of assistance from neighbouring countries, Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had informed the cabinet that there had been some developments.
"However, there are several aspects of coordination that need to be followed up on.
"The issue is that the fire has spread quite extensively.
"So, any form of assistance and assets that we offered about a month ago may now need to be reassessed to ensure that the assistance genuinely serves its intended purpose," Fahmi said.
He said discussions were ongoing, but details of the specific assets that might be sent were not yet available.

Title: Tougher penalties for illegal racing, tonto activities take effect today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tougher penalties for illegal racing, tonto (lookout) activities and vehicle document forgery took effect today under amendments to the Road Transport Act, the Transport Ministry said.
Under the new Section 42A, racing or testing speed on public roads is a specific offence, allowing enforcement action to be taken without waiting for an accident, injury or death to occur.
First-time offenders face a fine of RM2,000 to RM10,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both. For a second or subsequent conviction, the penalty increases to a fine of RM5,000 to RM20,000, imprisonment for up to five years, or both.
Section 110B addresses tonto activities, which involve obstructing enforcement operations, including following enforcement vehicles and leaking operational information to help others evade legal action.
Those convicted face fines of RM10,000 to RM50,000, imprisonment for one to five years, or both. The offence is also classified as an arrestable offence.
Amendments to Section 53B strengthen the accountability of registered vehicle owners for offences detected by enforcement cameras, including automated enforcement systems.
"The changes aim to close loopholes that could allow owners to evade responsibility for offences committed using their vehicles," the ministry said in a statement.
Amendments to Section 108 also increase penalties for forgery involving vehicle records, documents and information, including offences involving cloned vehicles and the manipulation of vehicle identities.
For certain offences, offenders face fines of up to RM200,000, imprisonment for up to 10 years, or both.
The ministry said the Act contains 42 amendment clauses aimed at improving road safety, strengthening enforcement and modernising Road Transport Department (RTD) services in line with technological developments and current needs.
The amendments also strengthen the legal framework for digital RTD services, including the electronic use of licences, documents, records and notices.
They will facilitate vehicle and driver licensing and enable digital accident reporting, subject to prescribed procedures, the ministry said.
Vehicle safety regulations will also be streamlined to cover electric vehicles, modified vehicles, vehicle components and micromobility vehicles.
Provisions governing cross-border vehicles have been strengthened to allow enforcement action against those that fail to meet legal requirements or have unresolved outstanding matters, the ministry said.
Meanwhile, the increase in the maximum compound limit for compoundable offences from RM300 to RM500 will take effect only on Jan 1, 2029.
The delay is intended to give road users sufficient time to adjust and is in line with the government's commitment when the Bill was tabled in parliament.
"The higher limit, however, does not mean all traffic offences will automatically incur a RM500 compound. The amount imposed will depend on the type of offence and the rules prescribed under the Road Transport Act.
"The measure aims to improve compliance and strengthen deterrence rather than burden the public or increase government revenue," it said.

Title: Four men arrested over Pekan Forest Reserve fire
Article:
PEKAN: Police have detained four men suspected of causing a large-scale fire at the Pekan Forest Reserve here on Monday.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Zaidi Mat Zin said the men, aged between 27 and 60, were pineapple farmers in the area.
He said they were detained to assist in investigations into the fire at a peat swamp forest adjacent to their residential area. However, they were released on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 285 of the Penal Code for negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter.
Meanwhile, Pahang Forestry Department deputy director (Development) Harry Yong said the fire at the Pekan Forest Reserve last week had destroyed more than 80 hectares of peat swamp forest.
He said the department had constructed two drains spanning about 1,500 metres to prevent the fire from spreading further into the forest reserve.
"Yesterday's heavy rain is understood to have helped extinguish the fire. However, staff from the Pahang Forestry Department and the Fire and Rescue Department are continuing to monitor the area daily," he said.

Title: Bersama member wants action against those spreading khalwat allegations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) member wants the party to take civil legal action and lodge a police report against those accused of spreading defamatory allegations linking a senior party leader to a khalwat arrest case.
Bersama member for Wangsa Maju, Ahmad Fariz Abdullah, said legal action should be initiated against those who originated and spread the allegations, including social media account owners and news portals involved.
He claimed that the allegations were politically motivated and intended to tarnish the leader's reputation and the party's good name ahead of the Melaka election.
In a statement today, he also warned social media users against speculating about or sharing content containing the allegations.
"Today, I express my anger and condemn the irresponsible actions of any party attempting to link a senior party leader to a khalwat arrest case.
"This reckless act is a deliberate, malicious and vile smear campaign aimed at character assassination and completely destroying the reputation of the leader concerned and the good name of Bersama," he said.
Ahmad Fariz made the call amid speculation over the identity of the politician arrested by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) on suspicion of committing khalwat at about 6pm yesterday.
Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad was reported as saying that two people had been arrested under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995.

Title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 to families of Long Lellang helicopter crash victims
Article:
KUCHING: The Sarawak government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the five families of those killed in the Sept 8 Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg presented the contributions to the victims' next-of-kin at a handover ceremony at the Sarawak State Assembly complex today.
"The loss of a family member cannot be measured in monetary terms, but we can provide some measure of support, especially for their children.
"Earlier, we presented offer letters from Yayasan Sarawak to assist with the payment of school and university tuition fees for their children," he told reporters after the ceremony.
On Sept 8, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Long Lellang.
The victims were Alexson Adit Henry, Debra Moset, Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, Jessie Paya Jok and Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.

Title: Malaysian Bar calls for natural justice in Negri Sembilan crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar wants all parties to uphold the principles of natural justice in resolving the constitutional crisis in Negri Sembilan.
Its president, Anand Raj, said this included any moves allegedly aimed at removing the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
He said any attempt to compel Tuanku Muhriz to stop performing his duties or abdicate must comply with Article X(1) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959.
The provision states that such action can only be considered and decided upon after a thorough investigation by the lawful Undangs.
"The proclamation dated April 19, which was allegedly aimed at removing Tuanku Muhriz, was rejected by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) because it was invalid.
"There is no published record to prove that such an investigation was ever conducted, or that Tuanku Muhriz was allowed to respond to the allegations against him," he said in a statement today.
Anand said the principles of natural justice required anyone facing allegations to be informed of the case against them and given an opportunity to correct or rebut the claims before an adverse decision was made.
He said if ordinary citizens were entitled to protection against unlawful removal from office without a fair hearing, the Yang di-Pertuan Besar was entitled to the same protection.
"Any action that fails to comply with Article X(1) of the State Constitution is invalid.
"If the court is asked to rule on the issue, it may set aside any decision made in breach of these principles," he said.
Anand also raised several questions about developments in the crisis, including Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim's announcement on Sept 16 that Tuanku Muhriz had been removed based on the disputed proclamation.
He said the announcement raised questions because the previous Menteri Besar had reportedly said that the proclamation was invalid. The former office-holder had also disclosed that he signed the document under pressure and duress.
"The public has a right to know who allegedly exerted this pressure, how it occurred, why a police report was made, and why he subsequently supported the proclamation.
"The basis for the state executive council's action at the time in allegedly suspending the State Secretary and the State Legal Adviser on Sept 22 also raises questions," he said.
He said both officers were federal officers, while the appointments of the state executive council members involved had reportedly been revoked on Sept 20.
"The AGC has explained that both officers serve in the federal service and are not subject to the jurisdiction of the state exco.
"Following the revocation of the appointments of all state exco members by Tuanku Muhriz, the basis allowing the state government to continue operating also requires clarification," he said.
Anand added that the Malaysian Bar took note of the Conference of Rulers' statement on Oct 14, which called for differences in stance to be resolved in accordance with custom and law, guided by the provisions of the State Constitution.
He said the Malaysian Bar respected that position and reiterated that Article X(1) of the State Constitution was among the provisions that must be strictly followed.
On Sept 17, Ismail was reported to have confirmed the proclamation of Tuanku Muhriz's abdication as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, following a unanimous decision by the state executive council two days earlier.
Following this, the Negri Sembilan State Secretary was asked to gazette the proclamation in accordance with existing regulations.

Title: Japan's Nikkei snaps six-day losing streak as AI shares rebound
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average snapped a six-session losing streak on Friday as artificial intelligence-related shares rebounded, although gains were limited by caution ahead of corporate earnings reports and US midterm elections.
The Nikkei rose 1.39 per cent to 65,324.29 after a near five per cent drop in the previous session. The index fell 5.37 per cent for the week.
The broader Topix rose 1.67 per cent to 4,066 but fell 0.95 per cent for the week.
"The shares rebounded as investors bought back stocks after sharp losses in the previous session... there were no other factors for the gains," said Daisuke Hashizume, senior strategist at Daiwa Securities.
"Market players see little reason to buy shares aggressively ahead of the release of corporate earnings and the US midterm elections next month."
Markets are watching whether the election outcome will affect US President Donald Trump's proposals for US$5,000 payouts for US adults and higher military spending, said Hashizume.
In Japan, chip-making equipment maker Tokyo Electron rose 2.56 per cent, memory chip maker Kioxia gained 3.84 per cent and technology investor SoftBank Group rose 1.9 per cent.
Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest recouped early losses to end 0.55 per cent higher.
BayCurrent surged 17.25 per cent to become the top percentage gainer on the Nikkei after the consulting firm said it would use excess cash for investments and share buybacks.
Banks supported the Topix, with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Mizuho Financial Group rising 1.82 per cent and 1.72 per cent, respectively.
Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 83 per cent rose, 14 per cent fell and two per cent traded flat.

Title: Kelantan KPDN probes subsidised cooking oil supply chain
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is conducting further investigations to determine whether other parties were involved in the misappropriation of subsidised cooking oil, following the seizure of 4,127 kilogrammes of the controlled item in Kampung Chetok, Pasir Mas, yesterday.
Kelantan KPDN director Hanif Yusabra Yusuf said the investigation aims to uncover potential illicit activities involving the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods.
During the operation part of 'Ops Tiris 4.0 (Integrated) carried out at 8
pm, the Kelantan KPDN seized subsidised cooking oil valued at RM11,053.50, along with five vehicles, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM138,053.50.
"The operation, conducted by Kelantan KPDN's Intelligence and Special Action Unit (URTK) in collaboration with the Patrol Unit (MPV) of the Pasir Mas district police headquarters, resulted in two separate cases.
"The first case involved the seizure of 1,577 kilogrammes of subsidised cooking oil of various brands, along with a Toyota Unser, a Mitsubishi Pajero, and a Nissan Navara, with a total value of RM70,678.50," he said during a press conference at the Kelantan KPDN headquarters here today.
According to him, the second case involved the seizure of 2,550 kilogrammes of subsidised cooking oil, along with a Toyota Hiace and a Mitsubishi Pajero, with a total value of RM67,375.
"The seized cooking oil consisted of one-kilogramme packets of various brands, as well as five-kilogramme bottled cooking oil produced by local companies in Kelantan and other states."
"Previously, the act of gathering supplies of subsidised cooking oil from wholesalers and storing them at specific locations is believed to have been the modus operandi of the parties involved," he said.
Hanif said action has also been taken against individuals linked to both cases.
The cases are being investigated under Sections 21 and 20(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961, as well as Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations 1974.
These provisions relate to the possession of controlled goods with the intent to commit an offence, the unauthorised transfer of controlled goods to unlicensed premises, and the wholesale of controlled goods without a valid license.
He added that the Kelantan branch of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) will continue to intensify enforcement operations particularly in border areas to curb the misappropriation and smuggling of subsidised controlled goods, and to ensure that these supplies are not misused. — BERNAMA

Title: PetroChina to restart part of shuttered Dalian refinery in November, sources say
Article:
SINGAPORE: PetroChina is preparing to restart a mothballed crude oil processing unit in northeast China next month to replenish domestic fuel stocks until a replacement refinery is constructed, according to multiple industry and trade sources.
In July 2025, PetroChina, the listed arm of CNPC, shuttered the entire 410,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Dalian Petrochemical refinery, once the group's largest and most profitable, in line with Beijing's efforts to cut excess refining capacity and focus on producing higher value petrochemicals.
PetroChina previously planned to restart a 200,000 bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) at Dalian in mid-2026, but the plan was held back as the US-Israeli war with Iran disrupted crude supplies and sent prices surging.
The plan to restart the CDU gained traction in recent months as China has faced depleted crude and fuel stocks after months of reduced crude imports and refining output because of the supply disruptions.
The monthly crude feed for the restarted CDU is planned at 500,000 to 600,000 metric tons, said one of the sources, a person with direct knowledge of the matter. That is equal to about 122,000 to 146,000 bpd, or about two per cent of China's seaborne crude imports in September, and translates to an operating rate of roughly 61 per cent to 73 per cent of total processing capacity for the unit.
The refinery is expected to receive crude shipments from South America and the Middle East next week for the restart, said one of the trade sources, who was briefed on the restart process.
Another factor behind restarting the old Dalian plant is a delay in the planned startup of a US$10 billion new refinery complex under construction on a nearby island, said two of the sources, traders who were also briefed on the company's plans. The new site was expected to start in mid-2028, they said.
The startup of the new complex is expected in March 2029, according to a September 8 tender document reviewed by Reuters from state-owned pipeline operator PipeChina seeking technical services for pipe works related to the restart of the old Dalian refinery.
PetroChina did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent by email.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family stunned by suspect's call informing them of Customs officer's death
Article:
TUMPAT: The family of a 35-year-old Customs officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband at their home in the Kuala Lumpur International Airport quarters yesterday, were left stunned when the suspect told them she was dead.
The victim's elder brother, Hazwan Ibrahim, 38, said the suspect told him his youngest sister, Nor Hazwani Ibrahim, had died and that he would surrender to police.
He said the suspect had called him about 7.30pm yesterday and asked him to be a witness to their divorce.
When he returned the call 10 minutes later, the suspect told him Nor Hazwani was dead.
He was speaking to reporters at his home in Kampung Telaga Lanas here today.
Police confirmed yesterday that Nor Hazwani was found murdered at the KLIA quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA in Nilai.
Nor Hazwan said his youngest sister had filed for divorce in September and was scheduled to attend a hearing at the Tumpat Syariah Court on Nov 3.
He said he had advised his sister and her husband to maintain an amicable relationship despite their marital problems.
"I understood that they were in the process of getting a divorce after my sister filed the application in September," he said.
Hazwan said he last met Nor Hazwani, the youngest of nine siblings, at her home yesterday before returning to Kelantan.
He said the couple had two daughters, aged 5 and 6, who had yet to be informed of their mother's death.
The family expects the victim's body to be brought back to Kelantan tomorrow after the post-mortem examination is completed.
It was reported that a female officer from the Customs Department was
found murdered
at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters, with her husband named as the suspect.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad confirmed that the police received information regarding the incident around 8.30pm.

Title: 14 arrested, 10 test positive for drugs in Temerloh R&R operation
Article:
TEMERLOH: Fourteen people were arrested, including 10 men who tested positive for methamphetamine, during an integrated multi-agency operation at the Temerloh Rest and Recreation (R&R) stop along the East Coast Expressway last night.
A total of 139 summonses were also issued during the operation.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said three men were arrested by the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department after testing positive for methamphetamine.
He said the National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) screened 68 people, with seven men testing positive for the same drug.
"Four other arrests involved an Indonesian man and three Bangladeshi nationals suspected of immigration offences.
"All 14 people have been processed," he said when met at the scene.
The four-hour operation, which began at 8pm, involved inspections of 371 vehicles and 388 people.
Also present was Pahang Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Superintendent Suresh Subramaniam.
Nasyim said the most common offence recorded was the use of non-compliant registration number plates, which resulted in 45 summonses, followed by speeding (43 summonses) and expired motor vehicle licences (12 summonses).
He added that the Road Transport Department issued 96 notices, while the Department of Environment issued two compound notices and three notices directing vehicles to undergo re-tests.

Title: China central bank chief touted yuan assets to investors, Bloomberg News reports
Article:
BEIJING: China's central bank governor Pan Gongsheng touted yuan assets to investors at a closed-door event in Bangkok and outlined plans to expand their role in global markets, Bloomberg News said on Friday, citing some who attended.
Pan highlighted the resilience of Chinese assets, particularly government bonds, and the diversification they can bring to investment portfolios, the report said.
Pan cited data showing a portfolio of 80 per cent yuan bonds and 20 per cent Chinese equities delivered a larger annual return over two decades than a global asset portfolio, the report added.
The yuan portfolio also had lower volatility than global benchmarks over five and 10 years, the People's Bank of China chief said.
Pan promised to align rules for yuan bonds more closely with global standards and promote their acceptance as eligible collateral at major international clearing houses, according to the attendees.
Governments and state entities are increasingly raising funds outside dollar-denominated bonds, including in local currency markets such as the Chinese renminbi, as competition for capital raises issuance costs, Citi's global head of public sector group Stephanie von Friedeburg told Reuters on Thursday.

Title: UN report warns global biodiversity action off track, urges implementation
Article:
YEREVAN (Armenia): UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Thursday launched the first global assessment report on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, warning that global efforts remain off track to meet the 2030 targets despite widespread national commitments.
The State of Biodiversity Action report, released in the Armenian capital of Yerevan ahead of the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), evaluates collective progress under the landmark framework adopted in December 2022, which sets out 23 targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030 and four long-term goals for 2050.
According to the report, nearly 90 per cent of the CBD's 196 Parties have established national biodiversity targets, close to 60 per cent have developed national biodiversity strategies and action plans, and over 70 per cent have submitted national reports.
Indigenous peoples and local communities, subnational governments, businesses and civil society organisations have also registered around 5,000 commitments.
However, such widespread engagement has not yet translated into sufficient progress.
None of the 23 global targets presents a fully positive picture, and fewer than half of the national targets assessed by Parties are currently on track, the report found.
While national targets address an average of 22 of the 23 global targets, many fail to cover their full scope.
For instance, far fewer countries have committed to reducing harmful subsidies under Target 18 than promoting positive incentives, and current national pledges under Target 3 fall well short of the goal to conserve 30 per cent of land and sea by 2030.
The report identified gaps in financing and other means of implementation, whole-of-government and whole-of-society action, as well as data and knowledge needed to track progress.
Targets requiring action beyond environment ministries — including business action, sustainable consumption, harmful incentives and finance — are among those lagging furthest behind.
"The report shows that many of the critical elements of progress, including finance, capacity, cooperation and data, are still missing in action," Guterres said.
"Nature won't thrive on good intentions."
The UN chief called for greater financial and technical support, particularly for developing countries, the reform of harmful subsidies, nature-positive investment, and stronger integration of biodiversity across public policies and budgets.
"The very biodiversity we depend on needs tangible progress, not more promises," Inger Andersen, executive director of the UN Environment Programme, said in the report's foreword, urging immediate action to overcome implementation challenges.
The report will inform the first global review of collective progress under the framework at COP17, scheduled for Oct 19 through 30 in Yerevan. — BERNAMA
