Title: ‘Until he retracts, go away’: Tuanku Muhriz rebukes Negeri Sembilan MB in public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, publicly reprimanded Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim as the state’s constitutional crisis drags on.
Videos circulating on social media show the ruler telling a group of people that Ismail had written to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal to say that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar.
A visibly angry Tuanku Muhriz then asked why the menteri besar wanted an audience with him.
“Why does he want to see me? Until he retracts what he said earlier, go away,” he said, before turning to address Ismail directly.
“Don’t see me, I don’t want to see you. You understand? I am the Yang Dipertuan Besar but you said I am not.”
Ismail responded with the angkat sembah, the customary gesture of greeting royalty.
Worshippers at the mosque were heard chanting “Daulat Tuanku” after the reprimand.
Negeri Sembilan has been gripped by a royal crisis since April, when four individuals claiming to be undang, or chieftains, declared that Tuanku Muhriz had been removed as ruler.
In June, the same disputed undang purportedly proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the “new” Yang Dipertuan Besar at a five-star hotel in Melaka.
Last month, Ismail endorsed a statement by his state executive council that purportedly affirmed Tuanku Muhriz’s removal. The ruler later revoked the appointments of the entire state executive council.

Title: Heavy downpour triggers flash floods across Kuching, roads and Sarawak Plaza basement swamped
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — Several areas in Kuching were hit by flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon.
Flooding was reported at Sarawak Plaza, the Mile 3 underpass, Jalan Tun Jugah and Jalan Batu Lintang after the rain began at around 1.30pm.
The downpour was accompanied by strong winds, with a tree also reportedly uprooted near Wisma Naim here.
Meanwhile, a video posted on Threads, filmed from a restaurant on the basement floor of Sarawak Plaza, showed workers trying to sweep away floodwater.
As of 2.45pm, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had forecast thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of Sarawak until 7pm.
The affected areas included Kuching, Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman, Betong, Mukah, Sarikei, Sibu, Kapit (including Song, Bintulu, Limbang and Miri. — The Borneo Post

Title: Malaysia’s fury rises as Indonesian haze shuts schools, blankets region, and sparks calls for accountability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Closed schools, shuttered sports centres and mass mask handouts. Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia.
“You need to treat them as an outcast in the region,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman railed this week talking about the Indonesian fires.
His comments go much further than the gentle diplomatic pressure Malaysia’s government has so far applied, but they reflect a simmering frustration with Indonesia’s inability to control the fires.
“Malaysia and Indonesia are close neighbours, but that relationship must also come with responsibility,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syerleena Abdul Rashid told AFP.
“Why should Malaysians continue paying the price for irresponsible actions beyond our borders?” she said.
Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Thursday defended the approach, saying the South-east Asian nation “has done everything we can” to engage neighbouring Indonesia on the issue.
‘Do the right thing’
But at the popular Batu Caves tourist site, visitors and workers alike expressed frustration.
“You cannot see,” tour operator Diddy Hamidon told AFP, looking out at a vista now shrouded in haze.
“The Indonesian (government) needs to do the right thing,” he added.
Malaysia has been forced to close schools over the haze, and has offered Indonesia help fighting the blazes.
But not until Wednesday did the offer appear to finally have been taken up, after talks involving disaster management officials on both sides, Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan said.
“The form of cooperation will depend on the outcome of the discussions,” he told local reporters.
“But the authorities of both countries have, for the first time, begun talks on how we can work together to tackle the haze, which appears to be getting worse.”
Indonesia experiences wildfires regularly during its annual dry season, but this year’s blazes have been exacerbated by a strong cycle of the El Nino weather phenomenon, which tends to bring drought to the country.
The fires have burned through hundreds of thousands of hectares in Indonesia and caused air pollution spikes in Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor, where schools closed this week due to the haze.
Haze shrouds Johor’s skyline across the Causeway, seen from Singapore on October 16, 2026. — AFP pic
The crisis is not the first caused by Indonesian fires, and in 2002, members of the Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) inked an agreement on transboundary haze pollution.
But that deal is widely seen as “not worth the paper it’s printed on,” said James Chin, professor of Asian studies at the University of Tasmania.
It has no enforcement mechanism, and previous efforts by Singapore to hold companies linked to wildfires legally culpable have also stalled.
Malaysia has asked Asean for an urgent meeting to discuss the latest crisis, and this year’s summit host Manila confirmed the issue will be on the agenda at a foreign ministers meeting next month.
“Asean members are more than willing to help,” Malaysian parliamentarian Hassan Abdul Karim told AFP, “provided Indonesia is willing to swallow their bigger ego and pride.”
Anger about Indonesia’s inability to control the haze was stoked further by comments over the weekend from Jakarta’s communications agency chief.
“We do not just send smoke... The oxygen in Singapore and Malaysia also comes from our forests,” said Syahganda Nainggolan in a video that swiftly went viral and prompted furious responses.
Syerleena called the remarks “downright insensitive”.
“We value our relationship with Indonesia, but that should not prevent us from speaking up when remarks are inappropriate,” said the parliamentarian.
Indonesia’s President Prabowo Subianto on Monday ordered the government to mobilise maximum efforts to battle wildfires that have been raging for three months in some places.
‘Very, very careful’
The growing public frustration in Malaysia but also neighbouring Singapore, which has topped global major city pollution rankings in recent days, is pressuring governments, said Chin.
But he forecast little progress.
“Asean is very, very careful when it comes to what they call domestic sovereignty. So they are unlikely to do anything,” he said.
Syerleena urged accountability at a regional level, with companies linked to burning held responsible whether they are Indonesian, Malaysian or Singaporean.
“What we need from Jakarta is greater transparency, stronger enforcement against companies responsible for illegal burning, and closer cooperation with neighbouring countries.” — AFP

Title: AAIB releases preliminary report on Long Lellang helicopter crash that killed five
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has published its preliminary report into the September 8 crash of a Flying Doctor Service helicopter at the Long Lellang STOLport in Miri, Sarawak, which killed a pilot and four passengers.
The Transport Ministry said the Bolkow BO105 S helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, was on a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight from Selungo to the Long Lellang STOLport at the time of the accident.
It said the report compiles the factual information identified at the early stage of the investigation, in line with the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability.
“Investigations are still ongoing to determine the cause and contributing factors of the accident,” the ministry said in a statement today.
It added that the information in the preliminary report is subject to change based on additional evidence, while a full analysis and the investigation’s conclusions will be detailed in the final report.
The ministry stressed that the investigation is aimed at preventing similar accidents, not at apportioning blame or liability to any party.
The investigation is being carried out in accordance with Annex 13 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation and the civil aviation regulations in force.
The ministry expressed its sorrow over the incident and conveyed its condolences to the families of the victims.
It also thanked the AAIB and all parties that assisted in the investigation, and said it remains committed to strengthening the country’s aviation safety.
The preliminary report can be downloaded at https://go.gov.my/Laporan-Insiden-Kemalangan-A11-26.

Title: Khazanah and PNB channelled nearly RM40m into FashionValet in 2018, court hears in Vivy Yusof trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Sessions Court here was told today that local fashion company, Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet), received investment funds totalling nearly RM40 million from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) eight years ago.
Tay Lay Hong, 54, a banking services manager at the Bukit Damansara branch of Public Bank, said the funds were deposited into a Public Bank account belonging to Fashion Valet through four separate transactions between March and December 2018.
“A review of Fashion Valet’s bank account statements revealed that Khazanah transferred RM7,848,000 on March 23, 2018, and RM11,742,000 on March 26, 2018, while PNB recorded transfers of RM11,953,500 on June 4, 2018, and RM8,364,996 on December 20, 2018,” she said.
The fifth prosecution witness said this in her witness testimony during the trial of Fashion Valet founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, who are facing charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB.
Tay also confirmed that a sum of RM11 million was withdrawn from Fashion Valet’s bank account on August 21, 2018, via an online ‘bulk payment’ transaction.
“This money transfer transaction, amounting to RM11 million, falls under a category of payments requiring verification specifically, approval from an ‘authorised person’ for the Public Bank account held in the name of Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd. However, I am not certain who the authorised person for online banking was.
“To my knowledge, the appointment of an authorised person is based on a Directors’ Resolution; typically, the authorised signatory is the same individual as the authorised person for online banking,” said Tay.
Furthermore, Tay who began her tenure with Public Bank in 1993 said a review of Fadzarudin Shah’s bank statements revealed an incoming transaction of RM5 million on September 4, 2018, from the company 30 Maple Sdn Bhd, with the reference “Interim Dividend”.
“I also reviewed the bank statements for the account held in the name of Vivy Sofinas Yusof, which showed an incoming transaction of RM5 million from 30 Maple Sdn Bhd on September 3, 2018, with the reference ‘CIMB Rentas’,” the witness testified.
According to Tay, a sum of RM5.5 million was withdrawn from each of the couple’s personal accounts at a Public Bank counter on September 5, 2018.
During cross-examination by lawyer Datuk M. Athimulan, the witness confirmed that all information contained in her witness statement was based on documentation, including bank statements.
Additionally, Tay agreed that the RM11 million withdrawn from the Fashion Valet bank account did not necessarily mean the funds were transferred into a single personal account; rather, it involved a ‘bulk’ [transaction]......the ‘payment’ was for items such as staff salaries, shop rental, and so forth.
Vivy, 38, and Fadzarudin, 37, are charged acting with common intention in their capacity as directors of Fashion Valet with criminal breach of trust involving investment funds from Khazanah and PNB. They allegedly authorised payments totalling RM8 million from a Fashion Valet corporate bank account to a company called 30 Maple, without the approval of the Fashion Valet Board of Directors.
The offence was allegedly committed at the Public Bank Berhad branch in Bukit Damansara (located at 36-40 Medan Setia 2, Plaza Damansara, Bukit Damansara) on August 21, 2018 under Section 409 of the Penal Code, read in conjunction with Section 34 of the same Code; if convicted, this carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term of not less than two years and up to 20 years, along with whipping and a potential fine.
They also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge: acting with common intention to dishonestly misappropriate property belonging to Fashion Valet specifically, the RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB at the same location and on the same date.
The couple is charged under Section 403 of the Penal Code, which carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term of not less than six months and up to five years, along with whipping and a mandatory fine, upon conviction.
The trial, presided over by Judge Rosli Ahmad, will resume on November 3. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 each to families of Flying Doctor Service crash victims
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — The Sarawak state government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the families of the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, which occurred on September 8.
Additionally, educational assistance is being provided through Yayasan Sarawak (Sarawak Foundation) to help ease the burden on the victims’ families, specifically by ensuring the continuity of their children’s education.
The contributions were presented by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to the next-of-kin of the five victims during a handover ceremony held at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly complex today.
“The loss of a family member cannot be measured in monetary terms, but we can provide some measure of support to them especially to their children.
“Earlier, we presented offer letters from Yayasan Sarawak to assist with the payment of school and university tuition fees for their children,” Abang Johari told reporters following the event.
On September 8, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, crashed near the Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Long Lellang.
The victims were Alexson Adit Henry, Debra Moset, Dr. Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, Jessie Paya Jok, and Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham. — Bernama

Title: Lawyers urge public to avoid speculation as Zara Qairina inquest heads to January ruling
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — Lawyers involved in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir have urged the public to avoid speculation and allow the judicial process to take its course following the conclusion of witness testimonies.
Lawyer Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers accused in the bullying case involving the Form One student, said she hoped the evidence presented during the inquest had been addressed comprehensively.
“We hope there will be no speculation and no unwarranted accusations against anybody, as this remains a tragedy for all the children whose lives have been deeply affected by this case.
“Justice must be guided by evidence and the rule of law, rather than public sentiment or speculation,” Goh told reporters on the sidelines of the proceedings at the Coroner’s Court here today.
Goh also stressed the need to protect the rights, welfare and future of the children involved, urging all parties to respect the legal process and allow them to move forward with their lives.
“The pursuit of justice for Zara must never come at the expense of justice for others, and our thoughts remain with the family over this tragic loss,” she said.
Meanwhile, lawyer Shahlan Jufri, representing Zara Qairina’s mother, said his team had several matters to address in its written submissions, which must be filed by December 15.
He said the coroner had asked all parties to assist the court in identifying discrepancies in witness testimonies and evidence, and to provide their views on the visit conducted at the school.
“The coroner also sought feedback and recommendations from all parties on improving future inquest proceedings, including school safety and investigation procedures,” he said.
Shahlan said his team would review 350 documentary exhibits and more than 5,000 pages of proceedings notes accumulated over the 96-day inquest before filing its submissions.
“We hope the court’s eventual decision will be fair to all parties,” he said.
The Coroner’s Court today fixed January 15 next year to deliver its findings on Zara Qairina’s death.
After 96 days of proceedings, the Coroner’s Court on Wednesday concluded hearing the testimonies of 83 witnesses, including experts, children, teachers and family members.
The inquest began on September 13 last year, with Queen Elizabeth Hospital forensic pathologist Dr Jessie Hiu called as the first witness and investigating officer Insp Wong Yew Zhung as the final witness.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) announced on August 13, 2025, that an inquest would be conducted into Zara Qairina’s death after reviewing the investigation report submitted by the police.
The decision followed the exhumation of Zara Qairina’s remains on August 9, 2025, at the Tanjung Ubi Muslim Cemetery in Kampung Mesapol, Sipitang, which was completed at 7.15pm to facilitate a post-mortem examination.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel in the early hours of July 16. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm AKPS officer killed in KLIA quarters domestic dispute, knife seized, husband remanded
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A woman was found dead after allegedly being stabbed by her husband at a Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters unit last night, believed to have stemmed from a domestic dispute.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received a report regarding the incident at about 9.30pm after a man surrendered himself at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi Police Station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported his wife’s death at their residence.
Acting on the information, a police team was dispatched to the scene, where they found a woman, in her 30s, unconscious.
He said initial investigations by the Negeri Sembilan D10 Forensic Division found that the victim sustained injuries suspected to be from being stabbed, while a knife along with several other pieces of evidence were also seized to assist in the investigation.
“The deceased was a customs officer who had been transferred to the Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), effective July 1,” he said in a statement today.
He said a medical team from the Nilai Health Clinic examined the victim at the scene and confirmed her death, and that police have arrested her husband, also in his 30s, to assist in the investigation.
Alzafny said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder and that the suspect has been remanded for seven days until October 22.
He also advised the public against making any speculation that could interfere with police investigations. — Bernama

Title: China agrees in principle to Malaysia’s proposal for world TVET council, says Zahid
Article:
TIANJIN, Oct 16 — China has agreed in principle to Malaysia’s proposal to establish a World Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Ahmad Zahid said the agreement which includes a proposal for China to serve as the permanent host was conveyed by his counterpart, Ding Xuexiang, and Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng during a meeting yesterday.
He noted that the proposal to establish the World TVET Council, with China acting as the permanent secretariat, was formally presented during his keynote address at the World Technical and Vocational Education and Training Development Conference 2026 (WVTEDC 2026) here today.
“I proposed it yesterday, and today I have officially put it forward in my speech. In terms of principle, Deputy Prime Minister Ding and China’s Minister of Education have agreed,” he said during a press conference following the event.
Ahmad Zahid, who also serves as the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, emphasised that the council is essential for creating a sustainable global platform to foster cooperation in skills development, technology, and workforce training, also expressed confidence in the initiative’s viability, citing China’s experience in organising TVET conferences over the past four years.
Ahmad Zahid, who also chairs the National TVET Committee, added that under this proposal, China would serve as the permanent secretariat to coordinate the sharing of knowledge and expertise within the TVET education ecosystem, thereby enabling member nations to benefit from ongoing collaboration.
The Deputy Prime Minister said the initiative also holds the potential to expand cooperation between TVET institutions in Malaysia and China including a proposed collaboration involving China’s “Luban Workshop” training centers, the Malaysia-China Institute (MCI), and various local TVET institutions.
Ahmad Zahid noted that such cooperation could pave the way for the implementation of skills training programmes, supporting Malaysia’s efforts to develop a highly skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of the job market.
He added that the participation of over 100 countries and the attendance of 48 ministers at the WVTEDC 2026 conference reflect a global commitment to the development of education and skills training.
“We hope that efforts to strengthen the nation’s TVET ecosystem will continue to receive support from all stakeholders, in line with our aspiration to produce a workforce that meets industry needs, as Malaysia strives to become a highly skilled nation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Tuanku Muhriz bestows state honours on three Undangs and their consorts
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, conferred the state’s prestigious honours on three Undangs and their consorts at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here yesterday.
The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office said in a statement today that the three Undangs - Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari of Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi of Luak Jelebu and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid of Luak Rembau — were conferred the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS).
Their consorts - Tok Puan Sharifah Amirah Ir Syed Ismail Ash-Shahab of Sungei Ujong, Tok Puan Datin Norazizan Mamat of Jelebu and Tok Puan Asmah Yaakob of Rembau - were honoured with the Darjah Mulia Negeri Sembilan (DMNS).
The statement said the DTNS was reserved for the four Undangs and the Tunku Besar Tampin, while the DMNS was reserved for their consorts.
Also present at the ceremony were the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.
Other attendees included State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim, State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal and State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali. — Bernama

Title: PKR to contest nine Melaka seats, Pakatan to unveil full line-up on Oct 24
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — PKR will contest nine state seats under Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the upcoming Melaka state election on November 14, party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said.
She said the names of PKR candidates, together with those from other PH component parties, would be officially announced by coalition chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 24.
Fuziah said the announcement would be made during the launch of the PH election machinery at the parking lot of Hang Jebat Stadium in Melaka at 8pm.
“PKR has committed to nine seats as part of PH’s efforts to mount a strong challenge in the Melaka polls.
“The party’s preparations for the state election are now in its final stages, with the candidate selection almost finalised,” she told reporters after the launch of the Southern Zone International Franchise Exhibition tour at the Paradigm Mall Convention Centre here today.
Fuziah was speaking in her capacity as deputy minister of domestic trade and cost of living.
She said PKR’s priority was to ensure all preparations were in place to mount a competitive challenge.
She added that the party would contest only under PH, as no formal political or electoral agreements had been made with other parties.
“Any strategy regarding potential cooperation with other parties are part of PKR’s internal planning.
“However, PKR welcomes any form of support from other parties wishing to assist the coalition for the upcoming Melaka state election,” she said.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional won two.
The Election Commission has set October 31 for nomination, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling, following the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly on September 23.

Title: New road transport law takes effect, illegal street racing now a specific offence
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport (Amendment) Act 2026, which amends the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333), came into force today, introducing new provisions to curb illegal street racing and ‘tonto’ syndicate activities, as well as strengthen enforcement and the digitalisation of Road Transport Department (JPJ) services.
The Transport Ministry (MOT) said the Act, which contains 42 amendment clauses, was part of the government’s efforts to improve road safety, strengthen enforcement and modernise JPJ service delivery.
According to the ministry, one of the key changes is the introduction of Section 42A, which makes racing or testing speed on public roads a specific offence.
“This provision enables enforcement action to be taken without having to wait for an accident, injury or loss of life to occur,” MOT said in a statement today.
For a first conviction, offenders may be fined between RM2,000 and RM10,000, or jailed for up to two years, or both.
For a second or subsequent conviction, offenders may be fined between RM5,000 and RM20,000, or jailed for up to five years, or both.
MOT said the Act also introduces Section 110B to address ‘tonto’ syndicate activities that obstruct or interfere with enforcement operations, including tailing enforcement vehicles and relaying information about operations.
“Those convicted of the offence may be fined between RM10,000 and RM50,000, or jailed for between one and five years, or both. The offence is also categorised as an arrestable offence,” it said.
The ministry said other amendments strengthen the accountability of registered vehicle owners for offences detected by enforcement cameras, including automated enforcement systems.
“These amendments aim to close legal loopholes that could allow certain parties to evade responsibility for offences committed using their vehicles,” the ministry said.
MOT said the amendments also strengthen the legal basis for the use of electronic licences, documents, records and notices, while paving the way for digital accident reporting in accordance with prescribed procedures.
In addition, regulations governing the safety of electric vehicles, modified vehicles, vehicle components and micromobility vehicles have been strengthened.
“MOT believes that the implementation of the amendments to Act 333 will strengthen enforcement agencies’ ability to curb activities that endanger road safety, while making public services more convenient through the use of technology and digital services,” it said.
The ministry further said the increase in the maximum compound limit for compoundable offences from RM300 to RM500 would take effect on Jan 1, 2029, to allow sufficient transition time for road users.
“MOT wishes to clarify that the increase in the maximum compound limit does not mean that all traffic offences will automatically incur a RM500 compound. The amount offered is subject to the type of offence and the rules prescribed under Act 333.
“The measure aims to improve legal compliance and provide a more effective deterrent, rather than burdening the public or increasing government revenue,” the ministry stressed. — Bernama

Title: School bus operators told to update driver records by Oct 30 for RM1,000 aid before Deepavali
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — All school bus owners and operators have been urged to update their drivers’ details from today until October 30 to facilitate the disbursement of RM1,000 in special financial assistance.
The Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) said in a statement today that the information could be updated through its official portal at https://bantuanpemandu.mot.gov.my/bas-sekolah.
The required information includes each driver’s current name, address, telephone number, valid driving and Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licences, and bank account number for payment.
APAD said the exercise was aimed at ensuring eligible school bus drivers receive the assistance as soon as possible, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s call for payments to be completed before Deepavali.
The agency said it had also engaged with the Federation of Malaysian School Bus Associations and the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor School Bus Operators Association to ensure an orderly and accurate eligibility verification and payment process.
As part of the process, drivers’ records will be cross-checked against databases maintained by APAD, the Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) and the Road Transport Department (JPJ).
This includes checking the validity of driving and PSV licences to ensure recipients meet the eligibility requirements.
Payments will be made in phases starting Oct 22.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke previously said about 53,000 taxi, hire car and school bus drivers were expected to receive a one-off payment of RM1,000 each before Deepavali. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak says RM1.5b interim grant not final, pushes for clear constitutional formula
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — The increase in the interim payment of the special grant to Sarawak to RM1.5 billion does not constitute a definitive solution, said Deputy Minister in the Sarawak Premier’s Department (Law, MA63 and State-Federal Relations) Datuk Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali.
She stressed that the Sarawak government would continue to push for a clear and consistent formula to be established under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution.
“For a long-term solution, the Sarawak government has proposed that a clear and consistent formula be established to determine the rate of the special grant.
“The proposed formula is still being discussed by the Sarawak and Federal governments, and no final formula has been agreed upon so far,” she said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
Sharifah Hasidah was responding to a question from Royston Valentine (GPS-Tellian) on the latest status of claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) following the interim special grant.
In response to a supplementary question on Sarawak’s stance in the event of a change in the Federal administration, she stressed that the state government would continue to champion Sarawak’s rights under MA63, regardless of who led the Federal government.
On September 16, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an increase in Sarawak’s interim special grant to RM1.5 billion, up from RM600 million previously, effective this year. — Bernama

Title: Sitiawan fire claims lives of two teenage sisters, homes and vehicles gutted in morning inferno
Article:
IPOH, Oct 16 — Two sisters were killed after being trapped in a fire that destroyed two adjoining double-storey houses in Kampung Koh, near Sitiawan, today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the two sisters were aged 15 and 18.
Sayani said the department received an emergency call at 9.01am, and personnel from the Sitiawan and Seri Manjung fire and rescue stations, as well as the Pantai Remis Volunteer Fire Brigade, arrived at the scene at 9.10am.
“They found the blaze involved two adjoining Class C houses measuring 40ft by 70ft each, which were almost 90 per cent destroyed, with the two sisters trapped inside,” she said in a statement today, adding that the fire also destroyed four vehicles and a motorcycle.
She said the operation was brought under control at 10.30am.
“The department’s K9 Special Team was also contacted to assist in the investigation. The bodies of both victims have been handed over to the police and taken to Teluk Intan Hospital,” she added. — Bernama

Title: Jais confirms two arrests in alleged khalwat case involving public figure
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 16 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) has confirmed the arrest of two people to assist investigations into an alleged khalwat case involving a public figure in Petaling Jaya yesterday,
Sinar Harian
reported.
Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said the arrests were made at about 6pm over suspected offences under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995.
Those convicted under the provision face a fine of up to RM3,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, he said in a statement today.
Mohd Shahzihan urged Muslims not to shame individuals by turning the matter into material for speculation, debate or slander, the Malay daily reported.
The case drew public attention after a post circulated on social media featuring a screenshot from closed-circuit television footage showing a Jais van in the car park of a premises.
According to the report, the post prompted questions about the presence of the religious enforcement vehicle, while the person allegedly seen entering the van was linked online to a senior leader of a political party.
The claims sparked speculation before Jais confirmed the arrests.
However, the department did not identify either individual detained.

Title: Budget 2027 debate dominates Dewan Rakyat as MPs tackle haze, health and school safety
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 was the main focus of the Dewan Rakyat in the second week of the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, alongside current issues such as haze, health, education and school safety, as well as the cost of living.
A total of 75 government and opposition Members of Parliament (MPs) debated the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage over four days, beginning Monday (Oct 12), following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9.
During the debate, Sabah and Sarawak MPs welcomed the increase in interim special grants to the two states from RM600 million to RM1.5 billion, but called for the final formula to be settled and for clarification on Sabah’s entitlement to 40 per cent of the federal government’s net revenue derived from the state.
Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) proposed the permanent establishment of an Asean Special Task Force on Forest and Land Fires (Karhutla), involving Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia, to address the transboundary haze crisis. He also proposed legal action to claim compensation if Indonesia refused to accept the assistance.
Welfare issues also came under the spotlight, with Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor (PN-Ketereh) urging the government to expedite the resolution of pension adjustments for Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans who retired before January 1, 2013.
Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) stressed that school safety and bullying must not be taken lightly. He proposed a special allocation to train teachers to identify early signs of emotional distress and potential violence among students, while ensuring that every school had an adequate number of counsellors and structured psychological assessment programmes for early intervention.
During the oral question-and-answer session, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the procurement of 400 new ambulances would enhance emergency response capabilities for critical cases. He said his ministry had also increased medical equipment supplies to address the effects of haze, including 841 adult AeroChamber inhaler spacers, 396 units for children and 576 nebulisers.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the government aimed to create 500,000 job opportunities through initiatives involving artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation and automation, while expanding high-growth, high-value industries and strategic sectors.
He said the government would also continue to stabilise the prices of essential goods through law enforcement, Jualan Rahmah Madani and Jualan Agro Madani, following the implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage from June 2027.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said 1,726 private housing projects involving 199,643 units, with a gross development value of RM158 billion, had been successfully revived as of August through the efforts of the Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects.
In the agriculture sector, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the government would look into targeted assistance for paddy farmers who suffered lower yields due to delays in fertiliser supplies, to identify those who had genuinely incurred losses.
Meanwhile, the Minister’s Question Time (MQT) session on Tuesday, during which the Prime Minister is scheduled to answer questions raised by MPs, was answered by the relevant ministers as the Prime Minister was attending an event at Istana Negara.
During the Special Chamber session, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the transboundary haze, which had affected the country’s air quality since August 8, was expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks due to changing wind patterns during the monsoon transition period.
On Wednesday, the Dewan Rakyat also approved the appointment of four MPs — Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) — to the Parliamentary Services Council through a voice vote without debate.
The week’s sitting also saw the first reading of the Adoption (Amendment) Bill 2026 on Thursday, which, among other things, proposed amending Section 2 of Act 257 to redefine “child” by lowering the age limit from 21 to 18.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 runs from October 12 to 22, followed by a four-day winding-up session by the relevant ministers beginning October 26.
The current Dewan Rakyat sitting will run for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

Title: Johor’s Pasir Gudang records API 207, highest nationwide as 30 areas hit unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 207, the highest in the country, while 30 other areas recorded unhealthy readings as of 9am today.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Johan Setia (185), Klang (181), Petaling Jaya (173), Shah Alam (171), Banting (169) and Kuala Selangor (155).
In Johor, besides Pasir Gudang, Larkin had an IPU reading of 194, followed by Pengerang (177), Batu Pahat (172), Kluang (171), Kota Tinggi (164), Tangkak (163) and Segamat (160).
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai recorded 189, Seremban 181 and Port Dickson 172; in Melaka, Bandaraya Melaka registered 179, Bukit Rambai 178 and Alor Gajah 172; while in Pahang, Temerloh had a reading of 155, Rompin 152 and Jerantut 122.
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda recorded an API reading of 170 and Cheras 168, while Putrajaya registered 174.
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded 169, Tanjung Malim 162, Pegoh 154 and Tasek, Ipoh 151; while in Sabah, Tawau had an unhealthy API reading of 152.
Meanwhile, 37 areas recorded moderate API readings. Readings of zero to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Coroner’s Court sets Jan 15, 2027 for verdict in Zara Qairina inquest
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — The Coroner’s Court here has set January 15 next year to deliver its decision on the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir.
Coroner Amir Shah Amri Hassan fixed the date today following discussions with all parties involved in the inquest.
He said the parties had been given until December 15 to file their written submissions.
Amir Shah also said that the court had fixed January 8, 2027, for the clarification of the submissions.
“The verdict will be delivered in Bahasa Melayu,” he said.
Amir Shah highlighted several important points that parties should include in their written submissions to assist him in reaching a decision, including any contradictions or inconsistencies in witnesses’ testimonies, particularly those involving child witnesses.
The coroner also asked the parties to provide an overview of the
locus in quo
or site visit conducted at the school, including their views on the school or hostel environment, the investigation process and the inquest proceedings.
He further invited the parties to identify any systems or processes that could be improved by the relevant authorities.
The Coroner’s Court on Wednesday concluded hearing the testimonies of all 83 witnesses, including experts, children, teachers and family members, after 96 days of proceedings in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina.
The inquest into the death of the Form One student commenced on September 13 last year, with Queen Elizabeth Hospital forensic pathologist Dr Jessie Hiu as the first witness and investigating officer Insp Wong Yew Zhung as the final witness, who testified on Wednesday (October 14).
On August 13, 2025, the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) announced that an inquest would be conducted into Zara Qairina’s death after reviewing the investigation report submitted by police.
On August 8, 2025, the AGC said that Zara Qairina’s remains would be exhumed to allow for a post-mortem examination.
The exhumation at the Tanjung Ubi Muslim Cemetery, Kampung Mesapol, Sipitang, was completed at 7.15pm on August 9, 2025.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel in the early hours of July 16. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak formulates proposals to improve Flying Doctor Service, strengthen Medevac and rural health delivery
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — Sarawak is exploring ways to improve healthcare delivery to remote communities following the suspension of its Flying Doctor Service (FDS) after a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, that claimed five lives on September 8.
Deputy Minister of Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang said alternative healthcare delivery methods would be used temporarily while the government formulates proposals to improve the service’s safety and effectiveness.
He said mobile clinic teams were being deployed via four-wheel-drive vehicles and boats to accessible areas, while emergency medical evacuations (Medevac) were being coordinated through alternative government air assets.
These include the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Air Unit, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Air Wing and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
“The government will continue to evaluate and improve the methods of delivering healthcare services to rural areas, taking into account aspects of safety, effectiveness and service continuity, to ensure that rural communities continue to have access to the necessary healthcare services,” he said.
Tiang was responding to Krian assemblyman Friday Belik during the question-and-answer session at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting here on Friday.
He said the government was formulating proposals for a comprehensive improvement of the FDS, covering operational safety, aircraft suitability and capability, emergency training and preparedness, personnel welfare and protection, as well as alternative methods of delivering healthcare to rural communities.
The measures would take into account the findings of relevant assessments and investigations, as well as healthcare needs in remote localities.
Tiang also said the Sarawak State Health Department, in collaboration with JBPM, was organising the Sarawak Medevac Staff Engagement, Safety Briefing and Aircraft Familiarisation Roadshow 2026.
The initiative aims to strengthen medical personnel’s understanding, preparedness and confidence in Medevac operations and patient escorts to ensure evacuations are carried out safely and efficiently.
Tiang described the September 8 crash as a tragedy that deeply affected Sarawak, particularly the healthcare fraternity and the families of the five victims, comprising four healthcare personnel and a helicopter pilot.
He conveyed the Sarawak government’s condolences to the bereaved families and paid tribute to the victims for their service to communities in remote areas.
Introduced in Sarawak in 1973, the FDS provides primary healthcare, maternal and child health services, and emergency medical evacuations to communities inaccessible by road.
Tiang said the service had played an important role for decades in overcoming the geographical challenges faced by communities in Sarawak’s interior.
He stressed that the government would continue to assess appropriate service delivery methods to ensure healthcare access was maintained while prioritising safety and effectiveness. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak state assembly suspends DAP’s Chong Chieng Jen over offensive language, unverified claims in Budget debate
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — Chong Chieng Jen (DAP-Padungan) has been suspended for the remainder of the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting for misleading the House and making unsubstantiated allegations while debating the 2027 Sarawak Budget.
Transport Minister and Senadin assemblyman Datuk Seri Lee Kim Shin yesterday moved the motion to suspend Chong, which was passed with 62 votes in favour, one against and one abstention.
DUN Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohd Asfia Awang Nassar announced that the suspension took effect immediately and would remain in force until the sitting concludes on October 21.
Chong was absent during the tabling of the motion because he was in Parliament.
Lee said Chong had persistently used and repeated information and allegations which he had not verified or could not justify when asked by the Speaker to provide supporting evidence or justification.
He said the DAP Sarawak chairman had used offensive and insulting language against members of the House, and had imputed improper motives to other members or made statements or allegations which the said member was not prepared to substantiate.
“Every member of this House has the right to speak, to question, to disagree and to scrutinise the government. These are essential features of parliamentary democracy, and they must be respected.
“Those rights, however, carry responsibilities. Every member must observe the Standing Orders, respect the authority of the Chair, and exercise care in making statements and allegations in this House,” he said.
Lee said the motion refers to a statement made by Chong who uttered “And more importantly if such basic pagination of the document, that can such a serious error, what confidence do we have in the more detailed figures in the document budget?” recorded at page 15 of the unedited Hansard on October 13, which was alleged to have deliberately misled the House.
“It also concerns the Honourable Member’s conduct during the Budget debate on October 14, which we can find in yesterday’s Hansard from page 35 to page 44, particularly, I quote here: “So Tuan Speaker, you have wasted a lot of my time. I know you’re in control of this, please be fair to me.” as stated on page 38, including the reputation of information and allegations whose truth or accuracy he could not justify when called upon by the chair.
“The use of offensive and insulting language about members at page 40 of yesterday’s unedited Hansard, and I quote: “Kota Sentosa is hallucinating. He thought, you know, something criminal is being committed and the imputation of improper motives without substantiation,” he said.
Before putting the motion to a vote following a debate by members of the august House, Asfia said Chong’s speeches on October 13 and 14, as recorded in the Hansard, had flagrantly violated the Standing Orders.
He cited Standing Orders 32(4), 32(6), 32(10)(d) and 32(12), which cover the use of language deemed out of order, imputations of improper motives or unsubstantiated allegations against other members, the use of unverified information, and statements that deliberately mislead the House.
Quoting Standing Order 32(6), Asfia said no member could impute improper motives to another member or make any statement or allegation that he was not prepared to substantiate.
He also referred to Standing Order 32(10)(d), which prohibits members from using information, allegations or comments from any source, including newspapers, online newspapers, social media and other online platforms, if their truthfulness or accuracy could not be verified.
Asfia further cited Standing Order 32(12), which provides that any member who deliberately misleads the House is deemed to be out of order or in contempt.
He also invoked Standing Order 40(10), which states that nothing in the Standing Orders deprives the House of the power to proceed against any member in accordance with a resolution of the House.
During his State Budget debate on October 14, Chong had questioned the RM300 million lease of a pre-owned jet by the state government, alleging a lack of proper procurement procedures and a possible conflict of interest. — The Borneo Post

Title: Man with 33 criminal, drug records arrested over glue tin attack on elderly man in Segamat
Article:
SEGAMAT, Oct 16 — A 70-year-old man sustained a forehead injury after he was allegedly struck with a tin of glue by a man outside a business premises in Jalan Mohd Yusof, Kampung Abdullah yesterday,
Sinar Harian
reported.
Segamat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Jumazanzahir Chek Ismail said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred after the victim confronted the suspect for allegedly making a commotion outside the premises.
The suspect allegedly retaliated by hitting the elderly man on the head with the tin before fleeing the scene, he said in a statement today.
According to the Malay daily, the victim received treatment at Segamat Hospital for a cut to his forehead.
Police subsequently arrested a 40-year-old local man believed to be involved in the incident following intelligence gathered by the Segamat district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division.
Police also seized a tin of glue, a shirt and a pair of jeans to assist investigations.
Mohd Jumazanzahir said checks found that the suspect had 33 previous records involving criminal and narcotics offences, while an initial urine screening test returned negative for drugs.
He added that the suspect admitted to his involvement in the incident during further questioning.
Preliminary investigations indicated that the incident was believed to have stemmed from the suspect’s anger at being reprimanded by the victim.
The suspect was also believed to have been intoxicated at the time, he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code.
Police were to apply for a remand order at the Segamat Magistrate’s Court today to facilitate further investigations.

Title: MPs demand tougher Asean haze response, call for disaster fund and stricter enforcement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has proposed the establishment of a permanent Asean task force to tackle the transboundary haze crisis, in cooperation with Singapore, the Philippines, and Indonesia.
Debating the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage in the Dewan Rakyat today, Lim (PH-Bagan) said the task force must be supported by a permanent, year-round rescue team ready to act immediately when forest fires occur.
He said if Indonesia continues to reject the task force over sovereignty concerns, Malaysia would have no choice but to initiate legal action to claim compensation.
“Malaysians cannot just remain silent in the face of this haze crisis without taking any action,” he said.
He added that the current crisis stemmed from increasingly severe forest and land fires, claiming that the affected area in Indonesia had reached 300,000 hectares this year — 70 per cent larger than in 2023.
Lim also urged the government to provide special financial assistance to those affected by the haze, particularly gig economy workers and e-hailing drivers who were forced to stop work due to the unhealthy air quality.
During the same debate, Datuk Ali Biju (PN-Saratok) urged the government to explore international legal mechanisms to seek compensation from parties responsible for the transboundary haze, including commercial plantation companies involved in open burning.
He said the recurring haze not only affected the health of millions in the Asean region but also impacted tourism, businesses, transport, and the hosting of international sporting events.
Ali voiced concern that the haze could disrupt the 2027 SEA Games in Sarawak, scheduled for September next year, as the phenomenon usually occurs during that period.
“This haze is a man-made disaster. It is predictable, deliberate, and continues to occur every year,” he said.
He urged the government to lodge a formal complaint with Indonesia, strengthen laws on transboundary haze pollution, and consider setting up a disaster fund to help those affected.
Ali also called for stricter enforcement against parties conducting open burning.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting continues on Monday. — Bernama

Title: School assessment postponed as haze sparks MOE move to prioritise student health and safety
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The End-of-Academic-Session Assessment (UASA), scheduled to take place next week, has been postponed due to the haze currently affecting the country.
In a statement yesterday, the Ministry of Education (MOE) announced that this decision was made after taking into account the concerns of parents and guardians regarding the health and safety of their children specifically those required to attend school to sit for the assessment.
According to the Ministry, as the UASA is a school-based assessment, schools are granted the flexibility to reschedule the assessment dates.
“The new schedule will be communicated to parents and guardians,” the statement read.
MOE also acknowledged the dilemma faced by parents and guardians, who must balance their children’s health with the need to ensure they do not miss the assessment.
“MOE understands the dilemma faced by parents. They wish to protect their children’s health, yet are simultaneously concerned that absence from school might cause their children to miss the assessment,” the statement noted.
The Ministry emphasised that the health and safety of students remain the top priority, while also ensuring that the assessment process can be carried out in an orderly manner. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL: Cable theft attempt halts power on Kajang Line for an hour, police report lodged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — An attempted cable theft between the Phileo Damansara and Pusat Bandar Damansara stations disrupted MRT Kajang Line services early this morning.
Rapid KL said the incident was detected at 5.30am, following an intrusion into the track area.
It said power supply to the affected area was temporarily cut in line with established operating and safety procedures.
“This step was taken to allow the Auxiliary Police to carry out inspections and operations to track down the suspects safely, while ensuring the safety of passengers, staff and the track area as well as the smooth operation of train services,” it said in a statement today.
Power was restored at 6.32am after the necessary action was taken.
Rapid KL said alternative train services were provided temporarily throughout the inspection and search operation to ensure passengers could continue their journeys safely.
The operator said it viewed cable theft seriously as it could affect train services as well as the safety of passengers and staff.
A police report has been lodged at the Brickfields district police headquarters for further investigation.
Rapid KL added that it will continue to work with the Royal Malaysia Police to assist in the investigation and prevent similar incidents from recurring.

Title: MOH says mask up, avoid outdoor activity as haze blankets Malaysia with unhealthy air
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The public is advised to wear N95 face masks if they need to engage in outdoor activities during the haze, due to their ability to filter fine particles sized 2.5 microns (PM2.5) that can enter the respiratory system and harm health.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) said that if N95 face masks are unavailable, the use of three-ply face masks can be considered as a limited additional protection measure.
According to MOH, wearing appropriate face masks is crucial to reduce exposure to air pollutants, especially when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100, which is at an unhealthy level.
The ministry emphasised that the most effective step to minimise the adverse health effects of haze is to avoid outdoor activities when air quality reaches that level.
“However, if it is necessary to conduct activities outdoors, the public is advised to use appropriate face masks,” according to the statement yesterday.
MOH said this advice was issued following the haze situation hitting several areas in the country over the past few weeks, with air pollution levels fluctuating according to location and current conditions.
“MOH urges the public to remain vigilant, reduce exposure to the haze, and prioritise their own and that of their family’s health,” according to the statement.
The ministry stated that 35 air quality monitoring stations recorded API readings at the Unhealthy level (101 to 200), involving nine states and two Federal Territories based on Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) readings at 2pm yesterday.
Johor recorded the highest number of affected areas with eight areas, followed by Selangor (six), Perak and Pahang (four each), and Negeri Sembilan and Melaka with three areas each.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur and Sarawak each recorded two areas, while Putrajaya, Terengganu, and Sabah each recorded one area. However, MOH informed that no areas recorded API readings at the Very Unhealthy or Hazardous levels.
MOH stated that it will continue to monitor the haze situation and its impact on residents’ health, besides ensuring that health facilities, medicine supplies, and medical personnel are always ready to provide the necessary services.
The public can obtain further information on health prevention and protection measures during the haze through the MOH website at https://infosihat.moh.gov.my/isu-semasa/51-jerebu.html. — Bernama

Title: AKPS officer allegedly killed by husband was in divorce proceedings, says brother
Article:
NILAI, Oct 16 — The family of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband at a staff residential complex near Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) is struggling to come to terms with her death, her eldest brother said.
According to
Sinar Harian
, Amran Ibrahim, 59, said he initially could not believe the news that his youngest sister, Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, had been stabbed to death, allegedly by her husband.
He said he received a call from another brother at about 7.30pm yesterday informing him that Norhazwani had been killed and that her husband had surrendered to police.
Amran said he then contacted the police station, which confirmed that his sister had died after being stabbed.
He described Norhazwani, the youngest of nine siblings, as a cheerful person who rarely shared her problems with the family.
However, the family knew she had been experiencing marital problems and was in the process of divorcing her husband, he said, according to the Malay daily.
Amran also said Norhazwani’s husband had been released from prison a few days earlier after serving time for a drug-related offence.
It was earlier reported that the victim was a former Royal Malaysian Customs Department officer who had switched her service scheme to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) with effect from July 1.
A day before the incident, another brother who lives in Kelantan had stayed overnight at Norhazwani’s home. Amran said the couple appeared to be on normal terms, and his brother had advised them to maintain their relationship and avoid arguments.
Norhazwani and her husband had been married for seven years and had two children, aged five and six. The children are now being cared for by another sister in Kelantan, he reportedly said.
Amran told
Sinar Harian
that the family was deeply saddened by the incident and would leave the investigation and any further action to the police.
The victim’s body was taken to Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital in Seremban for further procedures. Amran said the family had been informed that a post-mortem would be conducted on Saturday morning, after which her remains would be taken to her hometown in Kelantan for burial.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad had earlier confirmed the incident, saying police received information about it at about 8.30pm yesterday.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

Title: Pending assemblyman hints Sarawak election may fall on Dec 12 or Dec 19
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — Pending assemblyman Violet Yong believes the next Sarawak election will be held either on December 12 or December 19, this year.
She made the remarks when concluding her debate speech on the State Budget 2027 at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting today.
“Until we meet again in the next term of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) after the state election, which is going to be held soon and my guess is on the 12th or 19th of December,” she told the DUN.
When asked to clarify what had triggered her to make such remarks, the Sarawak DAP Secretary said it was her way to say “Thank You” to the Deputy Speaker Datuk Idris Buang for presiding over the session.
On Sept 22, DUN Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Asfia Awang Nasar told reporters that this DUN session would be the last of the current term, paving the way for the next state election.
However, the date for the dissolution of the DUN has yet to be announced.
The term of the 19th State Legislative Assembly will expire in February next year. — The Borneo Post

Title: Tuition teacher held over alleged sexual offences involving five male students in Bukit Jalil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — A tuition teacher has been arrested over alleged sexual offences involving five male students with police investigating separate reports involving teenage and child victims, the
New Straits Times
reported.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the alleged offences took place at the suspect’s home, which was also used as a tuition centre.
According to the English daily, he said five police reports had been lodged at the Bukit Jalil police station, with the first made on October 6, followed by another on October 10 and three more on October 11.
Fadil said police had conducted detailed investigations and recorded statements from the victims and their family members, as well as other relevant parties.
He added that the victims’ families, schools and the District Education Office had cooperated with the investigation.
According to the New Straits Times, the suspect has been arrested and remanded to assist police with further investigations, he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 377C of the Penal Code and Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act.

Title: Pan Borneo Sabah delays stem from multiple factors, not one party, says projects chief inspector
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — Delays in the Pan Borneo Sabah Highway Phase 1A project cannot be attributed to any single party, with technical, administrative and financial challenges all contributing to the slow pace of implementation, said Datuk Seri Salleh Mohd Said Keruak.
The Chief Inspector of Projects Sabah said it was unfair to place the entire blame on the Sabah government, stressing that the completion of the long-awaited highway required closer cooperation among all parties involved.
He said more than 70 per cent of the project involved upgrading existing Federal roads from two lanes to four, a process complicated by land acquisition, buildings, residential areas and the relocation of utility infrastructure.
“These are not straightforward works.
“They require careful planning, coordination and technical assessment to ensure that construction can proceed without further complications,” he said in a statement.
Salleh identified changes to the original designs that did not fully reflect actual site conditions as one of the main factors contributing to delays.
He said such changes required detailed scrutiny and coordination among consultants and technical experts appointed by the Works Ministry (KKR).
The process was further complicated when design modifications resulted in additional costs, which required technical assessments and financial approval from KKR and the Finance Ministry (MOF).
He said lengthy approval processes had also affected the smooth implementation of the project.
To prevent similar delays from recurring, Salleh called on KKR and MOF to establish a clearer and faster approval mechanism, particularly for variation orders (VOs) and adjustments to financial limits.
He said the mechanism should be incorporated into the original contracts or formalised through supplementary agreements to ensure that necessary changes could be approved more efficiently.
“Faster and clearer approval processes are essential to prevent administrative and financial bottlenecks from holding up work on the ground,” he said.
Salleh stressed that the project involved shared responsibilities among the Federal and Sabah governments, consultants, contractors and utility companies.
Each party, he said, should be assessed according to its respective authority and responsibilities rather than allowing one party to become the sole target of criticism.
“The people of Sabah do not need a culture of blaming one another. They want to see this highway completed,” he said.
He said the priority should be to strengthen cooperation, expedite decision-making and improve the efficiency of approval processes to ensure the project progressed without unnecessary delays.
“What matters now is reducing delays, accelerating implementation and completing the project for the benefit of the people of Sabah,” he said.
Salleh said all parties needed to focus on practical solutions and fulfil their respective responsibilities to ensure the highway could be completed as efficiently as possible. — The Borneo Post
